newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya tea production down by 28 pct Jan-June 1997.
newsitem.headline: Kenya tea production down by 28 pct Jan-June 1997.

text.p: Kenya's tea production fell by around 28 percent in the first six months of 1997 compared the same period last year on account of bad weather, leading brokerage company Africa Tea Brokers Ltd (ATB) said on Tuesday.
"The cumulative figure for 1997 (January-June) now stands at 96.73 million kg -- a decrease of 37.6 million kg or 27.99 percent over the previous year," ATB said in a statement.
The crop figure for June 1997 was 16.264 million kg, a fall of 1.634 million kg or 9.13 percent over the same month in 1996, it added.

ATB said although there were "fairly useful" rains in the Nandi and Kericho districts in the latter part of June, most growing areas remained cold and wet. It added that growth was inhibited and plucking rounds had been reduced.
"Currently, with slightly warmer temperatures, leaf intake will show a gradual improvement except in Sotik and areas east of the Rift (Valley) where crops remain very low," ATB said.

ATB said that five sales were held during the month of June when a total of 327,879 packages were sold at an average price of $1.96 per kg. Comparative figures for the same month last year were 336,458 packages at an average price of $1.37.
Pakistan, Egypt, Sudan, Yemen, Britain and South Africa were the main buyers of Kenyan tea in June, ATB said.

Last year Kenya was the world's leading exporter of black teas. That position is widely expected to be reclaimed by Sri Lanka this year. Kenya's production in 1996 was a record 257 million kg, according to official statistics.

Tea is second behind tourism as Kenya's main hard currency earner. Government officials expect less earnings from the sector on account of less production, which will put further pressure on Kenya after the IMF cancelled a key aid package.
In Malawi, Africa Tea Brokers said temperatures were warmer but conditions remained dry and leaf intake was still very low.
The brokers posted production in Malawi in January-June 1997 at 27.75 million kg compared to 26.92 million kg in the same period last year.
ATB said Uganda's production in January-May was 7.70 million kg from 6.60 million kg in that period last year.
In Zimbabwe, total production in the first third of 1997 was 8.29 million kg from 8.42 million in that period last year.

Output in the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius was shown at 700,000 kg in the first quarter of the year from 1.15 million kg in January-April last year. In Tanzania, output in January-April was 6.0 million kg from 6.6 million kg last year.
